- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion rule: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true if true is lower than 3-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 1–2% per day for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/1.00 spikes followed by 0.00/0.33 drops, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true price drop.
